newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chirac holds brief talks with Yeltsin in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Chirac holds brief talks with Yeltsin in Moscow.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac arrived in Moscow on Sunday for a brief meeting with President Boris Yeltsin that is likely to focus on the NATO-Russia treaty due to be signed in Paris in 10 days' time.

Chirac, who is on his way home to Paris after a four-day state visit to China, was expected to spend just over an hour with his Russian counterpart. Russian officials have said they may also discuss bilateral trade and economic issues.

Chirac, accompanied by his wife Bernadette and a delegation of about a dozen French officials, left the Vnukovo-2 government airport in a motorcade for a state residence close by, where he was to meet Yeltsin. Officials declined to name the venue.
Chirac was due to fly on to Paris at 9.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) and may speak to reporters before leaving.

The French president, who met Yeltsin in Moscow on February 2 for talks on NATO, has been one of the Western leaders most sympathetic to Russian fears raised by the planned expansion of the Western alliance into eastern Europe.

Russian and NATO negotiators announced a deal last week on a treaty laying down a new relationship between Moscow and its old Cold War adversary, which is expected this summer to issue membership invitations to former Soviet-bloc states including Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
The NATO-Russia Founding Act gives Moscow a say in NATO decisions affecting Russia and contains assurances that the West will not deploy nuclear and other arms further east.
